summary: This diff adds four new, self-contained Python CLI scripts (intent_engine.py, context_engine.py, plan_generator.py, learning_engine.py) plus two purely additive YAML docs; no existing code is modified beyond an append-only status block in the phase plan, and no .github/workflows/**, migrations/, schema.sql, auth/, or permission/payment/billing paths are touched, so the pre-classified tier1 label is correct. All SQL access uses parameterized queries (no injection risk) and all subprocess calls use list-form argv (no shell injection). I independently re-ran gap-report, list-sessions, list-plans, and list-reflections against the live production sqlite DB and confirmed the outputs match the worker's claimed evidence exactly, including the learning engine's real disable/re-enable of automation_rules.is_active for rule AR-b3ac3e967571 -- the 'verdict feeds back into real behavior' claim is genuine, not a self-report. The work is honestly scoped: it declines to build speculative generic NLU, correctly defers all compliance-tracker (separate repo) wiring to future PRs, and documents real read-only grounding of the TypeScript files it references. Minor non-blocking issues noted below.
issues: Test/demo artifacts from live-testing (rule AR-b3ac3e967571 'phase6-learning-engine-test-rule', session conv-phase6-test-1, plan 'phase6-demo-onboard-invoice', and 4 synthetic intent_unmatched_log rows including a 'real_pattern_detected' gap-report verdict) were left in the shared production superboss-register.sqlite rather than cleaned up after verification, and now pollute real gap-report/reflection output for any future caller.

The new scripts' docstrings claim to follow 'the same write-lock ... convention as capability_registry/automation_rules', but only capability_registry writes (via superboss-register.py's _write_lock()) actually use a cross-process lock -- automation_rule_engine.py and these four new scripts all write to the shared sqlite file with no locking beyond sqlite's default busy timeout, so the docstring overstates the guarantee (though this matches automation_rule_engine.py's own pre-existing convention, so it is not a new regression).
